question: To whom did Luke address his Gospel, stating that he wrote an orderly account so his reader might know the certainty of the things instructed?
opt1: Most excellent Theophilus
opt2: The high priest Caiaphas
opt3: Cornelius the centurion
opt4: Nicodemus the ruler
correct: Most excellent Theophilus
explanation: Luke explicitly dedicated his Gospel narrative to Theophilus. Luke 1:3 (KJV) - "It seemed good to me also, having had perfect understanding of all things from the very first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus,"

question: In the days of Herod, king of Judaea, of which priestly course was Zacharias, the father of John the Baptist?
opt1: The course of Zadok
opt2: The course of Abia
opt3: The course of Immer
opt4: The course of Bilgah
correct: The course of Abia
explanation: Zacharias served in the temple according to the priestly division of Abia. Luke 1:5 (KJV) - "There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judaea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth."

question: Where did the angel of the Lord appear unto Zacharias while he was executing the priest's office in the temple?
opt1: Standing on the porch of Solomon
opt2: Beside the brazen sea in the court
opt3: Standing on the right side of the altar of incense
opt4: Between the brazen altar and the porch
correct: Standing on the right side of the altar of incense
explanation: The angel appeared stationed beside the altar of incense. Luke 1:11 (KJV) - "And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense."

question: According to the angel Gabriel, in whose spirit and power would John go before the Lord to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children?
opt1: Moses
opt2: Elisha
opt3: Samuel
opt4: Elias
correct: Elias
explanation: Gabriel declared that John would fulfill the prophetic role in the spirit and power of Elijah (Elias). Luke 1:17 (KJV) - "And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord."

question: In the sixth month, to which city of Galilee was the angel Gabriel sent by God to a virgin espoused to Joseph?
opt1: Nazareth
opt2: Capernaum
opt3: Bethsaida
opt4: Cana
correct: Nazareth
explanation: Gabriel visited Mary in the Galilean city of Nazareth. Luke 1:26 (KJV) - "And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,"

question: What title did the angel Gabriel declare would be given to the Holy Thing that should be born of the Virgin Mary?
opt1: The Prophet of Israel
opt2: The Son of God
opt3: The Prince of Peace
opt4: The King of Glory
correct: The Son of God
explanation: The miraculous conception by the Holy Ghost designated the Holy One as the Son of God. Luke 1:35 (KJV) - "And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

question: What occurred when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary in the hill country of Juda?
opt1: A cloud of incense filled the house
opt2: Zacharias regained his speech instantly
opt3: The babe leaped in her womb, and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost
opt4: A chorus of angels appeared above the house
correct: The babe leaped in her womb, and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost
explanation: Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost as her unborn child leaped in response to Mary's voice. Luke 1:41 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, that, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost:"

question: In Mary's Magnificat, what did she rejoice that God had done to the hungry and the rich?
opt1: Given bread to the kings and sent the poor away
opt2: Brought prosperity to merchants and poverty to peasants
opt3: Sent rain upon both the wicked and the righteous
opt4: Filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich empty away
correct: Filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich empty away
explanation: Mary extolled the divine reversal accomplished by God's sovereign mercy. Luke 1:53 (KJV) - "He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away."

question: When the neighbors and cousins desired to name Elisabeth's child Zacharias after his father, what did Zacharias write upon a writing table?
opt1: His name is John
opt2: He shall be called Elias
opt3: Name him Immanuel
opt4: Let him be called Joseph
correct: His name is John
explanation: Zacharias confirmed the name commanded by the angel by writing it down. Luke 1:63 (KJV) - "And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all."

question: In Zacharias's prophetic song, what title did he give to the divine visitor who comes through the tender mercy of God to give light to them that sit in darkness?
opt1: The Sun of Righteousness
opt2: The dayspring from on high
opt3: The Bright and Morning Star
opt4: The Light of the Gentiles
correct: The dayspring from on high
explanation: Zacharias praised God for the dawn of the Messianic era. Luke 1:78 (KJV) - "Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us,"

question: Who was the Roman emperor whose decree went out that all the world should be taxed when Cyrenius was governor of Syria?
opt1: Tiberius Caesar
opt2: Claudius Caesar
opt3: Caesar Augustus
opt4: Nero Caesar
correct: Caesar Augustus
explanation: The universal census was decreed during the reign of Augustus. Luke 2:1 (KJV) - "And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed."

question: Why did Mary wrap her firstborn son in swaddling clothes and lay him in a manger?
opt1: Because the innkeeper forbade their entry
opt2: Because the temple gates were shut
opt3: Because they sought seclusion from the Roman guards
opt4: Because there was no room for them in the inn
correct: Because there was no room for them in the inn
explanation: The Christ child was laid in a manger due to the lack of lodging space. Luke 2:7 (KJV) - "And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn."

question: What praise did the multitude of the heavenly host sing together with the angel in the pastures of Bethlehem?
opt1: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men
opt2: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts, all the earth is full of his glory
opt3: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power and riches
opt4: Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty
correct: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men
explanation: The heavenly army celebrated God's glory and peace towards humanity. Luke 2:14 (KJV) - "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men."

question: What had been revealed unto the just and devout Simeon by the Holy Ghost concerning his death?
opt1: That he should die before the feast of the Passover
opt2: That he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ
opt3: That he should live to witness the rebuilding of the temple
opt4: That he should lead the priesthood in Jerusalem
correct: That he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ
explanation: Simeon received divine assurance that he would see the Messiah before passing away. Luke 2:26 (KJV) - "And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ."

question: What solemn prophecy did Simeon speak directly unto Mary concerning her own future grief?
opt1: Thou shalt be exiled from the land of thy fathers
opt2: Thy sons shall be taken captive into Babylon
opt3: Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also
opt4: Thy name shall be forgotten among the daughters of Zion
correct: Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also
explanation: Simeon prophesied the maternal sorrow Mary would experience at the Cross. Luke 2:35 (KJV) - "(Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also,) that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed."

question: Which prophetess of the tribe of Aser, the daughter of Phanuel, departed not from the temple but served God with fastings and prayers night and day?
opt1: Miriam
opt2: Huldah
opt3: Deborah
opt4: Anna
correct: Anna
explanation: Anna of the tribe of Asher gave thanks to God and spoke of the Child to all who looked for redemption. Luke 2:36 (KJV) - "And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity;"

question: How old was Jesus when his parents went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast of the Passover and he tarried behind?
opt1: Twelve years old
opt2: Ten years old
opt3: Thirty years old
opt4: Seven years old
correct: Twelve years old
explanation: Jesus attended the Passover at twelve years of age when this event took place. Luke 2:42 (KJV) - "And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast."

question: Where did Joseph and Mary find Jesus after three days of searching for him among kinsfolk and acquaintance?
opt1: At the pool of Siloam praying
opt2: In the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions
opt3: At the Sheep gate speaking to the elders
opt4: Walking upon the Mount of Olives alone
correct: In the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions
explanation: The young Jesus was discovered engaging the theological doctors in the temple. Luke 2:46 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions."

question: What was Jesus' reply to his mother when she said, 'Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing'?
opt1: I am sent only unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel
opt2: The time is at hand, and the kingdom of God is near
opt3: How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
opt4: My hour is not yet come; return ye unto Galilee
correct: How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
explanation: Jesus affirmed His supreme devotion to His heavenly Father. Luke 2:49 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

question: In what four distinct areas did Jesus increase as he returned to Nazareth and was subject unto his parents?
opt1: Strength, fame, honor, and dominion
opt2: Knowledge, authority, power, and wealth
opt3: Righteousness, prophecy, grace, and majesty
opt4: Wisdom, stature, and in favour with God and man
correct: Wisdom, stature, and in favour with God and man
explanation: Scripture outlines Christ's comprehensive human growth and divine favour. Luke 2:52 (KJV) - "And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man."

question: In the fifteenth year of whose reign did the word of God come unto John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness?
opt1: Tiberius Caesar
opt2: Caesar Augustus
opt3: Claudius Caesar
opt4: Nero Caesar
correct: Tiberius Caesar
explanation: Luke anchors John's ministry chronologically to the reign of Emperor Tiberius. Luke 3:1 (KJV) - "Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the tetrarch of Abilene,"

question: From which Old Testament prophet's book did Luke quote when describing John the Baptist as 'The voice of one crying in the wilderness'?
opt1: Jeremiah
opt2: Esaias (Isaiah)
opt3: Ezekiel
opt4: Daniel
correct: Esaias (Isaiah)
explanation: Luke cites Isaiah 40:3-5 directly from the prophet Esaias. Luke 3:4 (KJV) - "As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight."

question: When John warned the multitudes that God was able to raise up children unto Abraham, from what did he say God could raise them?
opt1: The dust of the earth
opt2: The waters of Jordan
opt3: These stones
opt4: The trees of the forest
correct: These stones
explanation: John rebuked empty ancestral pride by emphasizing God's omnipotent creative power. Luke 3:8 (KJV) - "Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, That God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham."

question: What practical instruction did John give to the people when they asked him, 'What shall we do then?'
opt1: Offer three bullocks upon the altar
opt2: Fast twice in the week and tithe your herbs
opt3: Sell all your lands and flee to the mountains
opt4: He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise
correct: He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise
explanation: John demanded authentic fruits of charity and compassion. Luke 3:11 (KJV) - "He answereth and saith unto them, He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise."

question: What specific command did John the Baptist give to the publicans who came to be baptized?
opt1: Exact no more than that which is appointed you
opt2: Abandon your office and join the Levites
opt3: Pay double restitution unto every tax-payer
opt4: Do not collect taxes on the holy sabbath
correct: Exact no more than that which is appointed you
explanation: John instructed tax collectors to maintain honest civic stewardship without extortion. Luke 3:13 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you."

question: What three directives did John give to the soldiers who likewise demanded of him what they should do?
opt1: Flee military service, lay down weapons, and swear not
opt2: Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages
opt3: Guard the temple gates, protect the poor, and refuse Roman pay
opt4: Fast during campaigns, honor the centurion, and show no mercy to enemies
correct: Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages
explanation: John enjoined soldiers to avoid extortion, false accusations, and greed. Luke 3:14 (KJV) - "And the soldiers likewise demanded of him, saying, And what shall we do? And he said unto them, Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages."

question: With what two elements did John say the One mightier than he would baptize them?
opt1: Water and blood
opt2: Grace and truth
opt3: The Holy Ghost and with fire
opt4: Power and righteousness
correct: The Holy Ghost and with fire
explanation: John pointed forward to Christ's superior and purifying baptism. Luke 3:16 (KJV) - "John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire:"

question: Why was Herod the tetrarch reproved by John the Baptist before he added this evil to shut John up in prison?
opt1: For taking gold from the temple treasury
opt2: For allying with the king of Arabia against Rome
opt3: For violating the feast of the Passover in Caesarea
opt4: For Herodias his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done
correct: For Herodias his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done
explanation: John boldly rebuked Herod for his incestuous marriage and manifold wicked deeds. Luke 3:19 (KJV) - "But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother Philip's wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done,"

question: In what bodily shape did the Holy Ghost descend upon Jesus when he was baptized and praying?
opt1: Like a dove
opt2: Like a pillar of fire
opt3: Like cloven tongues of fire
opt4: Like an eagle
correct: Like a dove
explanation: The Holy Spirit visibly descended in the form of a dove. Luke 3:22 (KJV) - "And the Holy Ghost descended in a bodily shape like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased."

question: At the conclusion of Luke's genealogy of Jesus, to whom does the lineage trace beyond Seth and Adam?
opt1: Abraham
opt2: God
opt3: Noah
opt4: Melchizedek
correct: God
explanation: Luke's genealogy traces Christ's humanity all the way back to Adam, the created son of God. Luke 3:38 (KJV) - "Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God."

question: How many days was Jesus tempted of the devil in the wilderness while eating nothing?
opt1: Seven days
opt2: Twelve days
opt3: Forty days
opt4: Three days
correct: Forty days
explanation: Jesus underwent forty days of fasting and temptation in the wilderness. Luke 4:2 (KJV) - "Being forty days tempted of the devil. And in those days he did eat nothing: and when they were ended, he afterward hungered."

question: With which scripture from Deuteronomy did Jesus refute Satan's command to turn the stone into bread?
opt1: The Lord our God is one Lord
opt2: Man doth not live by bread only, but by every word of God
opt3: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart
opt4: It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God
correct: It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God
explanation: Jesus cited Deuteronomy 8:3 to defeat the devil's bodily temptation. Luke 4:4 (KJV) - "And Jesus answered him, saying, It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God."

question: When the devil took Jesus up into an high mountain and offered all the kingdoms of the world, what scriptural rebuke did Jesus give him?
opt1: Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve
opt2: Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity
opt3: The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof
opt4: Thou hast no power over the Son of man
correct: Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve
explanation: Jesus cited Deuteronomy 6:13 in commanding exclusive worship to God. Luke 4:8 (KJV) - "And Jesus answered and said unto him, Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve."

question: When the devil set Jesus on a pinnacle of the temple and urged him to cast himself down, what was Jesus' answer?
opt1: The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer
opt2: It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
opt3: He shall give his angels charge over me at all times
opt4: No sign shall be given unto this evil generation
correct: It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God
explanation: Jesus answered with Deuteronomy 6:16, refusing to presume upon God. Luke 4:12 (KJV) - "And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God."

question: In the synagogue at Nazareth on the sabbath day, which book was delivered unto Jesus to read?
opt1: The book of the prophet Jeremiah
opt2: The book of the Law of Moses
opt3: The book of the prophet Esaias
opt4: The book of the prophet Daniel
correct: The book of the prophet Esaias
explanation: Jesus was handed the scroll of the prophet Isaiah (Esaias). Luke 4:17 (KJV) - "And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,"

question: What common proverb did Jesus say the people of Nazareth would surely quote unto him concerning his works in Capernaum?
opt1: Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?
opt2: A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country
opt3: Physician, heal thyself
opt4: Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country
correct: Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country
explanation: Jesus anticipated their localized demands using the ancient proverb. Luke 4:23 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country."

question: Unto which widow in the land of Sidon was Elias (Elijah) sent when great famine was throughout all the land?
opt1: A woman that was a widow, unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon
opt2: A widow woman of Shunem
opt3: A woman of Samaria at the well of Sychar
opt4: A widow dwelling in Ziklag
correct: A woman that was a widow, unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon
explanation: Elijah was sent past the widows of Israel to the Gentile widow of Sarepta. Luke 4:26 (KJV) - "But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow."

question: Which leper alone was cleansed in the time of Eliseus (Elisha) the prophet, though many lepers were in Israel?
opt1: Gehazi the servant
opt2: Naaman the Syrian
opt3: Hazael of Damascus
opt4: Benhadad the king
correct: Naaman the Syrian
explanation: Naaman the Syrian was the sole leper cleansed through Elisha's ministry. Luke 4:27 (KJV) - "And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian."

question: When the enraged people of Nazareth thrust Jesus out of the city, to what place did they lead him intending to cast him down headlong?
opt1: The high tower of the city wall
opt2: The rock of Rimmon in the wilderness
opt3: The brow of the hill whereon their city was built
opt4: The steep precipice of Mount Tabor
correct: The brow of the hill whereon their city was built
explanation: They attempted to throw Him down from the brow of the hill. Luke 4:29 (KJV) - "And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong."

question: With what affliction was Simon's wife's mother taken when Jesus entered into Simon's house?
opt1: She was stricken with a withered hand
opt2: She was sick of the palsy and bedridden
opt3: She had an issue of blood for twelve years
opt4: She was taken with a great fever
correct: She was taken with a great fever
explanation: Luke, the physician, specifically recorded her condition as a great fever. Luke 4:38 (KJV) - "And he arose out of the synagogue, and entered into Simon's house. And Simon's wife's mother was taken with a great fever; and they besought him for her."

question: By which lake was Jesus standing when the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, leading him to enter Simon's ship?
opt1: The lake of Gennesaret
opt2: The Dead Sea
opt3: The pool of Bethesda
opt4: The river Jordan
correct: The lake of Gennesaret
explanation: Jesus taught the multitude from a boat on the Lake of Gennesaret (Sea of Galilee). Luke 5:1 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret,"

question: What did Simon Peter say to Jesus when instructed to launch out into the deep and let down his nets for a draught?
opt1: Master, the day is spent and the winds are contrary
opt2: Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net
opt3: Lord, our ships are mended and cannot bear the weight
opt4: Rabbi, we know no fish dwell in these deep waters
correct: Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net
explanation: Peter obeyed despite a night of fruitless labor. Luke 5:5 (KJV) - "And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net."

question: What exclamation did Simon Peter make when he fell down at Jesus' knees after the miraculous catch of fish?
opt1: Truly thou art the King of Israel!
opt2: Increase our faith, Lord, that we may see greater wonders!
opt3: Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord
opt4: Command me that I come unto thee on the water!
correct: Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord
explanation: Peter was struck with holy awe at his own sinfulness before Christ's divine power. Luke 5:8 (KJV) - "When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord."

question: What commission did Jesus give to Simon Peter after the miraculous catch of fish?
opt1: Go thy way, and sell all that thou hast
opt2: Rejoice, for thy name is written in heaven
opt3: Build three tabernacles here upon the shore
opt4: Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men
correct: Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men
explanation: Jesus redefined Peter's life calling from catching fish to evangelizing souls. Luke 5:10 (KJV) - "And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men."

question: What command did Jesus give to the man full of leprosy after cleansing him with a touch?
opt1: Charge him to tell no man: but go, and shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded
opt2: Proclaim throughout Decapolis what great things God hath done
opt3: Return to thy household and offer a sacrifice of praise
opt4: Wash seven times in the pool of Siloam before sundown
correct: Charge him to tell no man: but go, and shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded
explanation: Jesus instructed the cleansed man to follow Mosaic law as a testimony. Luke 5:14 (KJV) - "And he charged him to tell no man: but go, and shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them."

question: How did the men carrying a man taken with a palsy bring him before Jesus when they could not find entrance by reason of the multitude?
opt1: They broke down the wooden door of the dwelling
opt2: They went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus
opt3: They carried him through a rear window on a stretcher
opt4: They waited until the congregation dispersed at eventide
correct: They went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus
explanation: Their persistent faith bypassed the crowd through the roof tiles. Luke 5:19 (KJV) - "And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus."

question: What did the scribes and Pharisees reason in their hearts when Jesus said to the paralytic, 'Man, thy sins are forgiven thee'?
opt1: This man speaks as the prophets of old
opt2: He hath unwashed hands and breaketh the tradition
opt3: Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?
opt4: He deceiveth the people by the prince of devils
correct: Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?
explanation: The religious leaders rightly recognized that forgiving sins is God's prerogative alone, failing to see Jesus' divinity. Luke 5:21 (KJV) - "And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?"

question: What publican sitting at the receipt of custom did Jesus call with the words, 'Follow me'?
opt1: Zacchaeus
opt2: Theophilus
opt3: Nicodemus
opt4: Levi
correct: Levi
explanation: Levi (Matthew) left his tax office immediately to follow Christ. Luke 5:27 (KJV) - "And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me."

question: What was Jesus' answer to the scribes and Pharisees when they murmured against his disciples for eating and drinking with publicans and sinners?
opt1: They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance
opt2: The Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath
opt3: Go and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy and not sacrifice
opt4: Let both grow together until the harvest
correct: They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance
explanation: Jesus defined His mission as reaching the spiritually sick. Luke 5:31-32 (KJV) - "And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."

question: According to Jesus' parable of wine and bottles, why must new wine be put into new bottles?
opt1: Lest the old bottles be washed and made clean
opt2: Else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish
opt3: Because the old wine is better for immediate drinking
opt4: Lest the elders reject the wine at the wedding feast
correct: Else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish
explanation: New wine ferments and requires flexible new wineskins. Luke 5:37 (KJV) - "And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish."

question: On the second sabbath after the first, what action of the disciples caused the Pharisees to ask, 'Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days?'
opt1: Drawing water from the well of Sychar
opt2: Healing the sick in the synagogue
opt3: Plucking the ears of corn, and rubbing them in their hands to eat
opt4: Carrying their traveling beds across the fields
correct: Plucking the ears of corn, and rubbing them in their hands to eat
explanation: The Pharisees construed rubbing grain in the hand as threshing on the Sabbath. Luke 6:1 (KJV) - "And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands."

question: What Old Testament incident did Jesus recount to justify his disciples' conduct on the sabbath?
opt1: Moses striking the rock at Meribah
opt2: Elijah being fed by ravens at the brook Cherith
opt3: Joshua marching around the walls of Jericho on the sabbath
opt4: David entering into the house of God and eating the shewbread
correct: David entering into the house of God and eating the shewbread
explanation: David ate the consecrated bread when in genuine physical need. Luke 6:3-4 (KJV) - "And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him; How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?"

question: What sovereign declaration did Jesus make regarding his relationship to the sabbath day?
opt1: That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath
opt2: That the sabbath was abolished from that day forward
opt3: That the priests alone have mastery over the sabbath
opt4: That the sabbath is greater than the temple of God
correct: That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath
explanation: Jesus declared His absolute Lordship over the Sabbath day. Luke 6:5 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath."

question: What physical ailment did the man in the synagogue have whom Jesus healed on the sabbath despite the scribes' and Pharisees' scrutiny?
opt1: He was blind from his mother's womb
opt2: His right hand was withered
opt3: He was bowed together and could in no wise lift up himself
opt4: He had a severe impediment in his speech
correct: His right hand was withered
explanation: Luke noted specifically that the man's right hand was withered. Luke 6:6 (KJV) - "And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered."

question: What did Jesus do prior to calling his disciples and choosing twelve from among them whom he named apostles?
opt1: He fasted in the wilderness for three days
opt2: He offered sacrifices in the temple at Jerusalem
opt3: He went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God
opt4: He consulted the elders of Nazareth in the synagogue
correct: He went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God
explanation: Jesus spent an entire night in prayer before naming His twelve apostles. Luke 6:12 (KJV) - "And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God."

question: In the Sermon on the Plain, what woe did Jesus pronounce upon those that are rich?
opt1: Woe unto you that are rich! for your gold shall perish with you
opt2: Woe unto you that are rich! for thieves shall break through and steal
opt3: Woe unto you that are rich! for you have neglected the poor
opt4: Woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation
correct: Woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation
explanation: Jesus warned the rich of having already received their earthly consolation. Luke 6:24 (KJV) - "But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation."

question: What did Jesus command his disciples to do unto them that curse them and despitefully use them?
opt1: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you
opt2: Shake off the dust of your feet against them
opt3: Call down fire from heaven to consume them
opt4: Deliver them unto the magistrates for judgment
correct: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you
explanation: Christ enjoined unconditional love and prayer for persecutors. Luke 6:28 (KJV) - "Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you."

question: What measure did Jesus promise would be given unto those who give generously?
opt1: Ten talents for every mite bestowed in secret
opt2: Good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over
opt3: An hundredfold of houses, lands, and earthly goods
opt4: A crown of gold and royal garments of fine linen
correct: Good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over
explanation: The Lord described abundant divine reciprocal blessing. Luke 6:38 (KJV) - "Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again."

question: In the parable of the mote and the beam, what must a man pull out of his own eye first before he can see clearly to pull out the mote in his brother's eye?
opt1: The speck of dust
opt2: The veil of blindness
opt3: The beam that is in thine own eye
opt4: The thorn in the flesh
correct: The beam that is in thine own eye
explanation: Self-examination must precede righteous correction of others. Luke 6:42 (KJV) - "Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother's eye."

question: Unto what did Jesus liken whosoever cometh to him, heareth his sayings, and doeth them?
opt1: A tree planted by the rivers of water that bringeth forth fruit
opt2: A wise king who built strong towers and conquered his foes
opt3: A city set on an high mountain that cannot be hidden
opt4: A man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock
correct: A man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock
explanation: The obedient disciple is founded immovably upon the rock. Luke 6:48 (KJV) - "He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock."

question: What reasons did the Jewish elders give to Jesus when pleading that the centurion was worthy of having his servant healed?
opt1: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue
opt2: For he hath offered sacrifices to the God of Israel
opt3: For he hath protected our people from Roman taxation
opt4: For he is a proselyte of righteousness in Capernaum
correct: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue
explanation: The Jewish elders commended the centurion's love for Israel and generosity. Luke 7:5 (KJV) - "For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue."

question: What notable testimony of humility and faith did the Roman centurion send by his friends to Jesus as he approached the house?
opt1: Lord, remember my alms and my service in Caesarea
opt2: Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed
opt3: Master, come down quickly ere my young servant die
opt4: Rabbi, lay thy hands upon him that he may recover
correct: Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed
explanation: The centurion trusted Christ's sovereign word without needing physical presence. Luke 7:6-7 (KJV) - "Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed."

question: What did Jesus declare to the people following him after marveling at the centurion's words?
opt1: Blessed are the Gentiles, for they shall inherit the kingdom
opt2: The faith of Caesar's soldiers shall judge the scribes
opt3: I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel
opt4: Verily this Roman soldier shall sit with Abraham at the feast
correct: I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel
explanation: Jesus extolled the centurion's unmatched faith. Luke 7:9 (KJV) - "When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel."

question: In what city did Jesus raise from the dead a young man who was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow?
opt1: Bethany
opt2: Chorazin
opt3: Jericho
opt4: Nain
correct: Nain
explanation: The resurrection of the widow's only son occurred at the gate of Nain. Luke 7:11-12 (KJV) - "And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people. Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her."

question: What words did Jesus speak to the dead young man as he touched the bier outside the city gate of Nain?
opt1: Young man, I say unto thee, Arise
opt2: Lazarus, come forth
opt3: Talitha cumi, maiden arise
opt4: Awake, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead
correct: Young man, I say unto thee, Arise
explanation: With divine authority Jesus addressed the deceased youth directly. Luke 7:14 (KJV) - "And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise."

question: What question did John the Baptist send two of his disciples to ask Jesus?
opt1: Why dost thou eat with publicans and sinners while we fast?
opt2: Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
opt3: Wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?
opt4: Where dwellest thou, that we may come and abide with thee?
correct: Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
explanation: John sent his disciples to ask Christ directly concerning His identity. Luke 7:19 (KJV) - "And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?"

question: What evidence did Jesus tell John's messengers to report back to John in prison?
opt1: How the Roman garrisons were confounded and kings trembled
opt2: How fire descended from heaven upon the mountains of Samaria
opt3: How that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached
opt4: How thousands gathered at the temple praising the Son of David
correct: How that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached
explanation: Jesus pointed to Messianic prophecies being fulfilled in His deeds. Luke 7:22 (KJV) - "Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached."

question: What comparison did Jesus make concerning John the Baptist's greatness among those born of women and the least in the kingdom of God?
opt1: John is greater than Solomon, yet lesser than Moses and Elijah
opt2: Among all priests, none hath greater authority than John the Baptist
opt3: John hath no equal among prophets, and all shall bow to his doctrine
opt4: Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he
correct: Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he
explanation: Jesus extolled John while elevating new covenant privilege in the kingdom. Luke 7:28 (KJV) - "For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."

question: In the house of Simon the Pharisee, what did the woman who was a sinner do to Jesus as he sat at meat?
opt1: Stood at his feet behind him weeping, washed his feet with tears, wiped them with the hairs of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with ointment
opt2: Poured oil upon his head from an alabaster box of spikenard and departed without speaking
opt3: Brought gifts of gold and frankincense and presented them at his table
opt4: Fell at the feet of the Pharisee pleading for intercession before Christ
correct: Stood at his feet behind him weeping, washed his feet with tears, wiped them with the hairs of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with ointment
explanation: The repentant woman demonstrated deep devotion and sorrow for sin. Luke 7:38 (KJV) - "And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment."

question: In the parable of the creditor which had two debtors—one owing five hundred pence and the other fifty—which did Simon rightly say would love him most when he frankly forgave them both?
opt1: The debtor who paid his pledge first
opt2: He to whom he forgave most
opt3: The debtor who owed fifty pence
opt4: Neither, for both remained debtors in secret
correct: He to whom he forgave most
explanation: Gratitude corresponds to the magnitude of forgiven debt. Luke 7:42-43 (KJV) - "And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most? Simon answered and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged."

question: Which woman is specifically named as having seven devils cast out of her as she ministered unto Jesus of her substance?
opt1: Joanna the wife of Chuza
opt2: Susanna
opt3: Mary called Magdalene
opt4: Salome the mother of Zebedee's children
correct: Mary called Magdalene
explanation: Mary Magdalene was delivered from seven demons and faithfully ministered to Jesus. Luke 8:2 (KJV) - "And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,"

question: Who was Chuza, whose wife Joanna ministered unto Jesus and his disciples of her substance?
opt1: The ruler of the synagogue in Capernaum
opt2: A centurion in Caesarea
opt3: A chief scribe in Jerusalem
opt4: Herod's steward
correct: Herod's steward
explanation: Joanna's husband Chuza held a prominent position in Herod's court. Luke 8:3 (KJV) - "And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance."

question: In the Parable of the Sower, what does the seed represent according to Jesus' own interpretation?
opt1: The word of God
opt2: The children of the kingdom
opt3: The faith of believers
opt4: The holy law of Moses
correct: The word of God
explanation: Jesus defined the seed directly as God's Word. Luke 8:11 (KJV) - "Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God."

question: According to Jesus' explanation, who comes and takes away the word out of the hearts of those by the way side, lest they should believe and be saved?
opt1: The deceitfulness of riches
opt2: The devil
opt3: The persecution of rulers
opt4: The cares of this life
correct: The devil
explanation: Satan snatches the seed from unresponsive wayside hearts. Luke 8:12 (KJV) - "Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved."

question: What did Jesus answer when told that his mother and his brethren stood without, desiring to see him?
opt1: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me
opt2: The foxes have holes, but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head
opt3: My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it
opt4: Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come
correct: My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it
explanation: Jesus prioritized spiritual kinship defined by hearing and doing God's Word. Luke 8:21 (KJV) - "And he answered and said unto them, My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it."

question: What piercing question did Jesus ask his disciples after he arose and rebuked the wind and raging of the water on the lake?
opt1: Why could ye not watch with me one hour?
opt2: O ye of little faith, why doubt ye the scriptures?
opt3: Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me?
opt4: Where is your faith?
correct: Where is your faith?
explanation: Following the calming of the storm, Jesus questioned their faith. Luke 8:25 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, Where is your faith? And they being afraid wondered, saying one to another, What manner of man is this! for he commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey him."

question: What name did the demoniac of the Gadarenes give when Jesus asked him, 'What is thy name?'
opt1: Legion: because many devils were entered into him
opt2: Beelzebub: the prince of darkness
opt3: Apollyon: the destroyer
opt4: Mammon: the spirit of greed
correct: Legion: because many devils were entered into him
explanation: The demoniac answered Legion due to the multiplicity of inhabiting devils. Luke 8:30 (KJV) - "And Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many devils were entered into him."

question: Into what animals did the demons beseech Jesus that he would suffer them to enter, which then ran violently down a steep place into the lake and were choked?
opt1: An herd of wild goats
opt2: An herd of many swine feeding on the mountain
opt3: A pack of wolves in the desert
opt4: A drove of wild asses on the rocks
correct: An herd of many swine feeding on the mountain
explanation: The demons entered the herd of swine, which perished in the lake. Luke 8:32-33 (KJV) - "And there was there an herd of many swine feeding on the mountain: and they besought him that he would suffer them to enter into them. And he suffered them. Then went the devils out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked."

question: For how many years had the woman had an issue of blood, who spent all her living upon physicians neither could be healed of any?
opt1: Seven years
opt2: Eighteen years
opt3: Twelve years
opt4: Thirty-eight years
correct: Twelve years
explanation: The woman had suffered twelve years with the incurable condition. Luke 8:43 (KJV) - "And a woman having an issue of blood twelve years, which had spent all her living upon physicians, neither could be healed of any,"

question: What did Jesus say to Jairus, the ruler of the synagogue, when one came from his house saying, 'Thy daughter is dead; trouble not the Master'?
opt1: The child is not dead, but sleepeth; let no man mourn
opt2: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me shall never die
opt3: Weep not; only have patience, and God shall be glorified
opt4: Fear not: believe only, and she shall be made whole
correct: Fear not: believe only, and she shall be made whole
explanation: Jesus encouraged Jairus to maintain unwavering faith in the face of death. Luke 8:50 (KJV) - "But when Jesus heard it, he answered him, saying, Fear not: believe only, and she shall be made whole."

question: What two things did Jesus give unto his twelve disciples when he called them together and sent them to preach the kingdom of God?
opt1: Power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases
opt2: Two coats each and purses filled with silver
opt3: Swords of iron and shields of brass
opt4: Scrolls of the Law and golden censers
correct: Power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases
explanation: Christ endowed the twelve with divine authority over demonic powers and sickness. Luke 9:1 (KJV) - "Then he called his twelve disciples together, and gave them power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases."

question: What was Peter's direct answer when Jesus asked his disciples, 'Whom say ye that I am?'
opt1: Elias the great prophet of God
opt2: The Christ of God
opt3: John the Baptist risen from the dead
opt4: The King of the Jews
correct: The Christ of God
explanation: Peter confessed Jesus' divine identity as the Christ of God. Luke 9:20 (KJV) - "He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God."

question: According to Jesus, what must any man do if he will come after him?
opt1: Forsake his father's house and build an altar
opt2: Tithe all his possessions and fast weekly
opt3: Deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me
opt4: Offer three bullocks in the temple of Jerusalem
correct: Deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me
explanation: True discipleship requires daily self-denial and taking up one's cross. Luke 9:23 (KJV) - "And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me."

question: Who appeared in glory with Jesus on the mount of Transfiguration, and what specific subject did they speak of?
opt1: Abraham and Isaac, speaking of the covenant of circumcision
opt2: David and Solomon, speaking of the glory of the temple
opt3: Enoch and Elijah, speaking of the translation to heaven
opt4: Moses and Elias, who spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem
correct: Moses and Elias, who spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem
explanation: Moses and Elijah spoke with Christ regarding His impending departure at Jerusalem. Luke 9:30-31 (KJV) - "And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias: Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem."

question: What voice came out of the cloud that overshadowed the disciples on the holy mount?
opt1: This is my beloved Son: hear him
opt2: Behold the Lamb of God which taketh away the sin of the world
opt3: I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again
opt4: Fear not, for the Lord of hosts is with you
correct: This is my beloved Son: hear him
explanation: The Father's voice affirmed the Son's preeminence. Luke 9:35 (KJV) - "And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him."

question: When the disciples disputed among themselves which of them should be greatest, what visual illustration did Jesus use to teach them?
opt1: He placed a grain of mustard seed in their hands
opt2: He took a child, and set him by him
opt3: He washed their feet with water from a basin
opt4: He pointed to the sparrows flying above
correct: He took a child, and set him by him
explanation: Jesus set a child beside Himself to teach that true greatness lies in humility. Luke 9:47-48 (KJV) - "And Jesus, perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him, And said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great."

question: When a village of the Samaritans did not receive Jesus, what did James and John ask permission to command, prompting Jesus' sharp rebuke?
opt1: That an earthquake swallow their village as Korah of old
opt2: That a plague of darkness fall upon all their dwellings
opt3: Wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
opt4: That Roman cohorts march against them with the sword
correct: Wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
explanation: James and John desired vengeful fire, misunderstanding Christ's saving mission. Luke 9:54-55 (KJV) - "And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did? But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of."

question: What reason did Jesus give for why he rebuked James and John's vengeful request against the Samaritans?
opt1: For the Samaritans are also descendants of Abraham
opt2: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God
opt3: For Elias alone possessed power over the elements of fire
opt4: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them
correct: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them
explanation: Jesus declared His fundamental mission of salvation rather than destruction. Luke 9:56 (KJV) - "For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. And they went to another village."

question: What did Jesus say concerning his own earthly condition when a certain man declared, 'Lord, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest'?
opt1: Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head
opt2: Silver and gold have I none, but peace I give unto you
opt3: He that followeth me shall suffer persecution from the rulers
opt4: My kingdom is not of this world, nor have I earthly possessions
correct: Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head
explanation: Jesus made clear the earthly privations accompanying true discipleship. Luke 9:58 (KJV) - "And Jesus said unto him, Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head."

question: What did Jesus declare about the man who puts his hand to the plough and looks back?
opt1: He shall stumble in the furrows of the field
opt2: No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God
opt3: He shall lose his reward on the great day of harvest
opt4: He is like salt that hath lost its savour
correct: No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God
explanation: Unyielding perseverance is essential for kingdom service. Luke 9:62 (KJV) - "And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God."

question: How many other disciples did the Lord appoint and send two and two before his face into every city and place whither he himself would come?
opt1: Twelve others
opt2: Forty others
opt3: Seventy also
opt4: One hundred and twenty others
correct: Seventy also
explanation: The Lord appointed seventy others to precede Him in ministry. Luke 10:1 (KJV) - "After these things the LORD appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come."

question: What observation did Jesus make to the seventy concerning the proportion between the harvest and the labourers?
opt1: The harvest is barren, and the fields are overgrown with thorns
opt2: The labourers are many, but the harvest is already spoiled
opt3: The harvest shall wait until the appointed season of rain
opt4: The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few
correct: The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few
explanation: Jesus urged prayer for more labourers in God's vast harvest field. Luke 10:2 (KJV) - "Therefore said he unto them, The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest."

question: What dramatic vision did Jesus recount when the seventy returned with joy saying that even devils were subject unto them?
opt1: I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven
opt2: I saw the heavens opened and the angels ascending
opt3: I saw the prince of darkness bound in chains of iron
opt4: I beheld the fiery lake prepared for the dragon
correct: I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven
explanation: Jesus described Satan's decisive overthrow as lightning falling from heaven. Luke 10:18 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven."

question: Instead of rejoicing that spirits were subject unto them, what supreme reason for joy did Jesus give to his disciples?
opt1: That ye have wrought signs in the presence of rulers
opt2: Because your names are written in heaven
opt3: That no venom of serpents can harm your flesh
opt4: That ye shall sit upon twelve thrones of judgment
correct: Because your names are written in heaven
explanation: Jesus taught that salvation in heaven transcends any spiritual authority or miracle. Luke 10:20 (KJV) - "Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven."

question: What question did a certain lawyer ask Jesus, tempting him regarding the inheritance of eternal life?
opt1: Which is the greatest commandment in the law of Moses?
opt2: Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?
opt3: Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
opt4: By what authority doest thou these miraculous works?
correct: Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?
explanation: The lawyer initiated the dialogue with a testing question about eternal life. Luke 10:25 (KJV) - "And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?"

question: Desiring to justify himself after reciting the summary of the Law, what follow-up question did the lawyer ask Jesus?
opt1: How often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him?
opt2: What good thing must I do that I may have eternal life?
opt3: Is the neighbor only of the circumcision?
opt4: And who is my neighbour?
correct: And who is my neighbour?
explanation: The lawyer sought to narrow the boundary of love with this question. Luke 10:29 (KJV) - "But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?"

question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, which two religious figures passed by on the other side without helping the wounded man?
opt1: A priest and a Levite
opt2: A Pharisee and a Sadducee
opt3: A scribe and a ruler of the synagogue
opt4: An elder and a publican
correct: A priest and a Levite
explanation: Both a priest and a Levite ignored the injured traveller. Luke 10:31-32 (KJV) - "And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side. And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side."

question: What two substances did the Samaritan pour into the wounded man's wounds as he bound them up?
opt1: Water and frankincense
opt2: Oil and wine
opt3: Balm of Gilead and vinegar
opt4: Myrrh and honey
correct: Oil and wine
explanation: The Samaritan applied oil to soothe and wine to disinfect the wounds. Luke 10:34 (KJV) - "And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him."

question: How much money did the Samaritan leave with the host of the inn on the morrow to care for the wounded traveler?
opt1: Thirty pieces of silver
opt2: Five shekels of gold
opt3: Two pence
opt4: Ten talents of silver
correct: Two pence
explanation: The Samaritan gave two pence (denarii) to cover ongoing lodging and care. Luke 10:35 (KJV) - "And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee."

question: What gentle correction did Jesus give to Martha when she complained that her sister Mary had left her to serve alone?
opt1: Let Mary assist thee first, then sit together at my feet
opt2: Why trouble ye the maiden whose heart is upright before God?
opt3: Labor not for the meat which perisheth, but for spiritual food
opt4: Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her
correct: Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her
explanation: Jesus affirmed Mary's singular devotion to listening to His word. Luke 10:41-42 (KJV) - "And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her."

question: What request did one of Jesus' disciples make of him after he ceased praying in a certain place?
opt1: Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples
opt2: Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us
opt3: Master, grant that we may sit at thy right hand and thy left
opt4: Lord, explain unto us the mystery of the kingdom of God
correct: Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples
explanation: The disciple desired instruction in prayer akin to John's disciples. Luke 11:1 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, that, as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples."

question: In the parable of the persistent friend who knocked at midnight, how many loaves of bread did he ask to borrow for his journeying friend?
opt1: Seven loaves
opt2: Three loaves
opt3: Five loaves
opt4: Two loaves
correct: Three loaves
explanation: He requested three loaves from his neighbour at midnight. Luke 11:5 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say unto him, Friend, lend me three loaves;"

question: Why did Jesus say the man in bed would rise and give the loaves to his midnight petitioner, even if he would not do so simply for friendship?
opt1: Because of his legal obligation under the Law
opt2: Because the magistrates would punish him in the morning
opt3: Because of his importunity
opt4: Because he feared the thieves on the road
correct: Because of his importunity
explanation: Relentless persistence (importunity) compelled the neighbor to grant the request. Luke 11:8 (KJV) - "I say unto you, Though he will not rise and give him, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth."

question: What supreme gift did Jesus declare the heavenly Father would give to them that ask him, surpassing earthly fathers who give good gifts to their children?
opt1: A double portion of wisdom and riches
opt2: Dominion over earthly kingdoms
opt3: Angels of protection round about them
opt4: The Holy Spirit
correct: The Holy Spirit
explanation: Luke highlights the Holy Spirit as the preeminent gift bestowed by the Father. Luke 11:13 (KJV) - "If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?"

question: By what instrument of divine power did Jesus say he cast out devils, proving that the kingdom of God was come upon them?
opt1: With the finger of God
opt2: With the rod of Moses
opt3: With the sword of the Spirit
opt4: With the voice of the archangel
correct: With the finger of God
explanation: Jesus declared that casting out demons by the finger of God manifested His kingdom. Luke 11:20 (KJV) - "But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you."

question: What response did Jesus give when a certain woman lifted up her voice and cried, 'Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the paps which thou hast sucked'?
opt1: She shall be called blessed among all women of the earth
opt2: Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it
opt3: Verily she hath received her reward in Israel
opt4: Behold, salvation is of the house of David
correct: Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it
explanation: True spiritual blessedness lies in hearing and obeying God's Word. Luke 11:28 (KJV) - "But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it."

question: What only sign did Jesus say would be given unto this evil generation?
opt1: The sign of the brazen serpent in the wilderness
opt2: The sign of Elijah's chariot of fire
opt3: The sign of Jonas the prophet
opt4: The sign of manna descending from heaven
correct: The sign of Jonas the prophet
explanation: Jonah's deliverance was the sole sign given to that generation. Luke 11:29 (KJV) - "And when the people were gathered thick together, he began to say, This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet."

question: Who did Jesus say would rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them, having come from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon?
opt1: The queen of Sheba
opt2: The king of Tyre
opt3: The elders of Nineveh
opt4: The queen of the south
correct: The queen of the south
explanation: The Queen of the South sought Solomon's wisdom, yet a greater than Solomon was present. Luke 11:31 (KJV) - "The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here."

question: What woe did Jesus pronounce upon the Pharisees regarding their meticulous tithing versus their neglect of weightier matters?
opt1: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God
opt2: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye give gold to the altar and neglect your aging parents
opt3: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye offer blood of bulls and refuse mercy to the widow
opt4: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye count your shekels on the sabbath day
correct: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God
explanation: Christ rebuked their external micro-tithing while neglecting divine justice and love. Luke 11:42 (KJV) - "But woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone."

question: What key did Jesus accuse the lawyers of having taken away, neither entering in themselves nor allowing them that were entering to go in?
opt1: The key of David
opt2: The key of knowledge
opt3: The key of the sanctuary
opt4: The key of salvation
correct: The key of knowledge
explanation: The religious experts obscured the true understanding of God's Word. Luke 11:52 (KJV) - "Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered."

question: When an innumerable multitude gathered, what did Jesus begin to say unto his disciples first of all regarding the leaven of the Pharisees?
opt1: Beware of the tradition of the elders
opt2: Beware of their long phylacteries
opt3: Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy
opt4: Beware of false prophets which come in sheep's clothing
correct: Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy
explanation: Jesus defined the corrupting leaven of the Pharisees as hypocrisy. Luke 12:1 (KJV) - "In the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy."

question: Whom did Jesus command his friends to fear, rather than those who kill the body and after that have no more that they can do?
opt1: Fear the Roman governor who possesseth the power of execution
opt2: Fear the scribes and priests who sit in Moses' seat
opt3: Fear the adversary who walketh about as a roaring lion
opt4: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell
correct: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell
explanation: Only God holds eternal sovereign power over body and soul. Luke 12:5 (KJV) - "But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him."

question: For what price were five sparrows sold, yet not one of them is forgotten before God?
opt1: Two farthings
opt2: A single mite
opt3: One penny
opt4: Half a shekel
correct: Two farthings
explanation: Even sparrows worth two farthings are intimately cared for by God. Luke 12:6 (KJV) - "Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?"

question: What did Jesus say to the man in the company who said, 'Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me'?
opt1: Render therefore unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's
opt2: Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
opt3: Give thy brother his portion and seek heavenly treasure
opt4: Let the elders of thy city adjudicate between thee and thy brother
correct: Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
explanation: Jesus refused to act as a civil probate arbitrator over covetous disputes. Luke 12:14 (KJV) - "And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?"

question: What did God say unto the rich fool who planned to pull down his barns and build greater to bestow all his fruits and goods?
opt1: Thy wealth shall be given unto the heathen
opt2: The moth and rust shall corrupt all thy grain
opt3: Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?
opt4: Thy barns shall burn with unquenchable fire
correct: Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?
explanation: The rich man's selfish presumption met abrupt divine judgment. Luke 12:20 (KJV) - "But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?"

question: What royal figure in all his glory was not arrayed like one of the lilies that neither toil nor spin?
opt1: David
opt2: Caesar
opt3: Herod
opt4: Solomon
correct: Solomon
explanation: Solomon's royal splendor was eclipsed by the natural beauty of God's flowers. Luke 12:27 (KJV) - "Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these."

question: What encouraging word did Jesus speak to his disciples concerning the Father's pleasure in bestowing the kingdom upon them?
opt1: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom
opt2: Be of good cheer, for ye have overcome the world
opt3: Rejoice and be exceeding glad, for great is your reward in heaven
opt4: Stand fast in the faith, for the kingdom of God is within you
correct: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom
explanation: The Father sovereignly delights to grant His kingdom to His little flock. Luke 12:32 (KJV) - "Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom."

question: What fundamental principle of divine accountability did Jesus establish regarding the servant who knew his lord's will?
opt1: Unto the firstborn alone shall double punishment be measured
opt2: For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more
opt3: He that knoweth not his lord's will shall escape without punishment
opt4: All servants shall receive thirty and nine stripes without distinction
correct: For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more
explanation: Accountability is strictly proportional to light and privilege received. Luke 12:48 (KJV) - "For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more."

question: What did Jesus say he was come to send on the earth, stating, 'and what will I, if it be already kindled?'
opt1: The sword of judgment
opt2: The water of life
opt3: Fire on the earth
opt4: The peace of heaven
correct: Fire on the earth
explanation: Christ's coming initiated a purifying and dividing fire upon the earth. Luke 12:49 (KJV) - "I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?"

question: Until what point did Jesus warn the adversary would be cast into prison if he did not agree with his adversary by the way?
opt1: Till the year of jubilee shall arrive
opt2: Till the judge pardons his debt in mercy
opt3: Till seven years of labor be accomplished
opt4: Till thou hast paid the very last mite
correct: Till thou hast paid the very last mite
explanation: Unforgiven guilt demands full and inexorable satisfaction. Luke 12:59 (KJV) - "I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite."

question: What solemn refrain did Jesus repeat twice concerning the Galileans slain by Pilate and the eighteen crushed by the tower in Siloam?
opt1: Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish
opt2: Their blood crieth from the ground for vengeance
opt3: They were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem
opt4: The day of vengeance of our God is at hand
correct: Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish
explanation: Jesus warned that all unrepentant sinners face sudden catastrophe. Luke 13:3 (KJV) - "I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish."

question: For how many years did the dresser of the vineyard say the owner had come seeking fruit on the barren fig tree and finding none?
opt1: Seven years
opt2: Three years
opt3: Ten years
opt4: Five years
correct: Three years
explanation: The owner had sought fruit for three consecutive years. Luke 13:7 (KJV) - "Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?"

question: For how many years had the woman in the synagogue been bowed together by a spirit of infirmity, unable in any wise to lift up herself?
opt1: Twelve years
opt2: Thirty-eight years
opt3: Eighteen years
opt4: Seven years
correct: Eighteen years
explanation: The woman had suffered demonic bondage for eighteen years. Luke 13:11 (KJV) - "And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself."

question: How did Jesus defend loosening the crippled woman on the sabbath against the indignation of the ruler of the synagogue?
opt1: By citing Moses' healing of Miriam from leprosy
opt2: By asserting the temple was holier than the synagogue
opt3: By arguing the woman had fasted throughout the day
opt4: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?
correct: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?
explanation: Jesus exposed their hypocrisy by demonstrating compassion to a daughter of Abraham. Luke 13:16 (KJV) - "And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?"

question: In the Parable of the Leaven, into how many measures of meal did the woman hide the leaven till the whole was leavened?
opt1: Three measures of meal
opt2: Two measures of meal
opt3: Five measures of meal
opt4: Seven measures of meal
correct: Three measures of meal
explanation: The leaven was hidden in three measures of meal. Luke 13:21 (KJV) - "It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened."

question: What command did Jesus give when one asked him, 'Lord, are there few that be saved?'
opt1: Follow the traditions of the elders with diligence
opt2: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able
opt3: Offer prayers three times daily toward the temple
opt4: Keep the feast of the Passover in Jerusalem
correct: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able
explanation: Jesus exhorted urgent, agonizing effort (striving) to enter the narrow gate. Luke 13:24 (KJV) - "Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able."
