question: What words will the master of the house say to those who plead, 'We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets'?
opt1: Bring forth the wedding garment that ye may enter
opt2: Ye were never numbered among the circumcised of Israel
opt3: I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity
opt4: Sit ye down at the lower end of the table
correct: I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity
explanation: Mere superficial familiarity cannot substitute for genuine righteousness. Luke 13:27 (KJV) - "But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity."

question: What animal did Jesus call Herod Antipas when certain Pharisees warned him that Herod desired to kill him?
opt1: That wolf
opt2: That viper
opt3: That dog
opt4: That fox
correct: That fox
explanation: Jesus referred to the sly, crafty Herod as 'that fox'. Luke 13:32 (KJV) - "And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected."

question: Why did Jesus declare that he must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following?
opt1: For it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem
opt2: Because the Romans have set a guard upon the Jordan
opt3: That all the cities of Decapolis may hear the gospel
opt4: Lest the Sanhedrin take counsel against him in Galilee
correct: For it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem
explanation: Jerusalem was the historical locus of prophetic martyrdom. Luke 13:33 (KJV) - "Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem."

question: Under what metaphor did Jesus express his longing to gather the rebellious children of Jerusalem together?
opt1: As an eagle fluttereth over her young
opt2: As a hen doth gather her brood under her wings
opt3: As a shepherd gathereth the lambs with his arm
opt4: As a mother comforteth her suckling child
correct: As a hen doth gather her brood under her wings
explanation: Jesus depicted His tender, protective love using the imagery of a hen gathering her brood. Luke 13:34 (KJV) - "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!"

question: What disease did the man have who was before Jesus in the house of one of the chief Pharisees on the sabbath day?
opt1: He was stricken with palsy
opt2: He had a leprosy on his forehead
opt3: He had the dropsy
opt4: He was deaf and dumb
correct: He had the dropsy
explanation: Jesus healed a man suffering from dropsy (edema) on the Sabbath. Luke 14:2 (KJV) - "And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy."

question: What argument from emergency pit-rescue did Jesus pose to the lawyers and Pharisees after healing the man of dropsy on the sabbath?
opt1: Which of you would leave his sheep in the thicket of thorns?
opt2: Who among you would not water his camel at the fountain?
opt3: Will not a man save his silver cup if it fall into the well?
opt4: Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?
correct: Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?
explanation: Jesus silenced their objections by appealing to common humane care for trapped animals. Luke 14:5 (KJV) - "And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?"

question: When bidden to a wedding feast, where did Jesus instruct the guest to sit, rather than seeking the highest room?
opt1: Go and sit down in the lowest room
opt2: Stand beside the entrance until invited by name
opt3: Sit among the servants and waiters
opt4: Sit midway between the honorable and the humble
correct: Go and sit down in the lowest room
explanation: Jesus urged humble self-effacement over ostentatious self-exaltation. Luke 14:10 (KJV) - "But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee."

question: What spiritual rule of exaltation and abasement did Jesus conclude from his wedding feast parable?
opt1: The humble shall receive double honor in this present world
opt2: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted
opt3: He that striveth for mastery must be temperate in all things
opt4: The first shall be rewarded and the last shall be forgotten
correct: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted
explanation: God reverses human pride and rewards genuine humility. Luke 14:11 (KJV) - "For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted."

question: When making a dinner or supper, whom did Jesus advise his host to invite instead of friends, brethren, kinsmen, or rich neighbors?
opt1: The scribes and rulers of the synagogue
opt2: The merchants and civic leaders of the city
opt3: The poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind
opt4: The traveling strangers and soldiers
correct: The poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind
explanation: True hospitality ministers to those who cannot reciprocate. Luke 14:13 (KJV) - "But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:"

question: At what specific time did Jesus promise that those who invite the poor and destitute will be recompensed?
opt1: In the year of jubilee
opt2: When the Messiah establishes his throne in David's city
opt3: In the temporal prosperity of their children
opt4: At the resurrection of the just
correct: At the resurrection of the just
explanation: The selfless giver receives ultimate reward at the resurrection of the righteous. Luke 14:14 (KJV) - "And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just."

question: In the Parable of the Great Supper, what excuse did the second invited guest give for begging to be excused?
opt1: I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused
opt2: I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it
opt3: I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come
opt4: I must bury my father before I can sit at meat
correct: I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused
explanation: The second excuse involved proving newly purchased oxen. Luke 14:19 (KJV) - "And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused."

question: What did the master of the house command his servant to do in the highways and hedges after the initial guests made excuses?
opt1: Compel the rulers to provide restitution for the feast
opt2: Compel them to come in, that my house may be filled
opt3: Close the city gates lest the unruly enter
opt4: Distribute the meats to the dogs in the street
correct: Compel them to come in, that my house may be filled
explanation: The master commanded loving urgency to fill his banquet hall. Luke 14:23 (KJV) - "And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled."

question: In illustrating the necessity of counting the cost of discipleship, what two examples did Jesus present to the multitudes?
opt1: A sower scattering seed and a fisherman casting nets
opt2: A merchant seeking pearls and a shepherd guarding sheep
opt3: A man intending to build a tower, and a king going to make war against another king
opt4: A builder digging deep and a master paying talents to servants
correct: A man intending to build a tower, and a king going to make war against another king
explanation: Jesus cited the example of building a tower to emphasize calculating the cost. Luke 14:28 (KJV) - "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?"

question: What did Jesus say concerning salt that has lost its savour?
opt1: It shall be burned in the kiln with unquenchable fire
opt2: It may be restored by mingling with new wine
opt3: It shall be kept in the storehouse until the feast
opt4: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out
correct: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out
explanation: Insipid salt is useless for seasoning or fertilization and is cast out. Luke 14:35 (KJV) - "It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear."

question: What complaint did the Pharisees and scribes murmur against Jesus when the publicans and sinners drew near to hear him?
opt1: This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them
opt2: He transgresseth the traditions of the elders by unwashen hands
opt3: He speaketh blasphemy against the temple and the law
opt4: He collecteth tribute for Caesar without authority
correct: This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them
explanation: The Pharisees despised Jesus for welcoming and eating with sinners. Luke 15:2 (KJV) - "And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them."

question: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep, where did the shepherd leave the ninety and nine while he went after that which was lost until he found it?
opt1: In the fold within the city
opt2: In the wilderness
opt3: Beside the still waters
opt4: Under the care of a hired keeper
correct: In the wilderness
explanation: The shepherd left the ninety-nine in the open pasture (wilderness) to pursue the one lost sheep. Luke 15:4 (KJV) - "What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?"

question: What occurs in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth?
opt1: The trumpet of judgment sounds throughout the heavens
opt2: A golden crown is prepared upon the altar
opt3: There is joy in the presence of the angels of God
opt4: The records of debt are sealed with fire
correct: There is joy in the presence of the angels of God
explanation: Heaven erupts in joy when a single sinner turns in repentance. Luke 15:10 (KJV) - "Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth."

question: How did the younger son spend his portion of goods after gathering all together and journeying into a far country?
opt1: He invested in trade caravans and lost it to robbers
opt2: He bought houses and lands in foreign cities
opt3: He loaned it upon usury to merchantmen
opt4: There wasted his substance with riotous living
correct: There wasted his substance with riotous living
explanation: The younger son squandered his entire inheritance on self-indulgent living. Luke 15:13 (KJV) - "And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living."

question: In his destitute condition during the mighty famine, what was the prodigal son sent into the fields to feed, desiring to fill his belly with the husks they ate?
opt1: Swine
opt2: Asses
opt3: Camels
opt4: Goats
correct: Swine
explanation: Feeding unclean pigs represented the lowest possible degradation for a Jewish youth. Luke 15:15-16 (KJV) - "And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him."

question: What realization came to the prodigal son when he finally 'came to himself' in the pig pasture?
opt1: The citizen owed him wages for feeding the swine
opt2: How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
opt3: His older brother would send money to redeem him
opt4: The famine would soon end and restore his fortune
correct: How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
explanation: He recognized the abundant generosity of his father's household. Luke 15:17 (KJV) - "And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!"

question: What did the compassionate father do when he saw his returning son yet a great way off?
opt1: Sent his servants to wash him at the gate before entering
opt2: Shut the doors of the estate until the son offered sacrifice
opt3: Had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him
opt4: Stood on the tower and demanded a public confession
correct: Had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him
explanation: The father demonstrated unconditional grace and loving embrace. Luke 15:20 (KJV) - "And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him."

question: What four gifts and provisions did the father command his servants to bring forth for his restored son?
opt1: A purse of gold, a silver trumpet, an ephod, and a sweet ointment
opt2: A golden crown, an ivory scepter, a chariot, and a white horse
opt3: A linen turban, a seal of authority, sandals of leather, and sweet spices
opt4: The best robe, a ring on his hand, shoes on his feet, and the fatted calf
correct: The best robe, a ring on his hand, shoes on his feet, and the fatted calf
explanation: The father bestowed full reinstatement and lavish honor upon his son. Luke 15:22-23 (KJV) - "But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:"

question: What bitter grievance did the elder brother voice against his father when he refused to enter the feast of celebration?
opt1: Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends
opt2: Thou hast divided my inheritance and given it unto harlots and strangers
opt3: The servants obey him rather than me who laboured in the field
opt4: Thou hast broken the covenant of our fathers by killing the fatted calf
correct: Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends
explanation: The elder brother manifested legalistic self-righteousness and bitter resentment. Luke 15:29 (KJV) - "And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:"

question: With what tender words did the father vindicate the joyful celebration over the restored younger son?
opt1: His sins are paid by his long labor among the swine
opt2: Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine. It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found
opt3: Thou shalt inherit double of all that remaineth in the house
opt4: Let no man speak of past offences, for the law of mercy is fulfilled
correct: Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine. It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found
explanation: The father reminded the elder son of unbroken fellowship and justified the celebration of spiritual resurrection. Luke 15:31-32 (KJV) - "And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine. It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found."

question: Of what wrongdoing was the steward accused to his master in the opening of the Parable of the Unjust Steward?
opt1: That he stole gold from the treasury
opt2: That he smote the menservants and maidens
opt3: That he had wasted his goods
opt4: That he conspired with foreign debtors
correct: That he had wasted his goods
explanation: The steward was charged with squandering his master's possessions. Luke 16:1 (KJV) - "And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods."

question: What did the unjust steward say within himself when told he could no longer be steward?
opt1: I will flee into the land of Egypt with my silver
opt2: I will appeal to the Roman governor for justice
opt3: I will gather an army of debtors and burn the storehouses
opt4: What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed
correct: What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed
explanation: The steward weighed his physical limitations and pride before strategizing for the future. Luke 16:3 (KJV) - "Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed."

question: To what amount did the unjust steward reduce the bill of the debtor who owed an hundred measures of wheat?
opt1: Fourscore (eighty)
opt2: Fifty
opt3: Twenty
opt4: Sixty
correct: Fourscore (eighty)
explanation: He wrote a twenty percent reduction, changing one hundred measures to fourscore. Luke 16:7 (KJV) - "Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore."

question: Why did the lord commend the unjust steward, despite his dishonesty?
opt1: Because he had enriched the poor of the city
opt2: Because he had done wisely
opt3: Because he repaid the debt from his own purse
opt4: Because he confessed his faults before the elders
correct: Because he had done wisely
explanation: The master commended the steward's shrewd foresight in preparing for his future. Luke 16:8 (KJV) - "And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light."

question: What principle of trustworthiness did Jesus declare concerning faithfulness in small matters?
opt1: A man must be tested with silver before he is trusted with gold
opt2: The ruler of many cities must first govern his own house
opt3: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much
opt4: Faithfulness in secret shall be rewarded in the presence of all
correct: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much
explanation: Integrity in minute duties tests and proves capacity for greater stewardship. Luke 16:10 (KJV) - "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much."

question: Which two masters did Jesus explicitly declare that no servant can serve simultaneously?
opt1: Caesar and the Sanhedrin
opt2: The Law and the traditions of the elders
opt3: The world and the flesh
opt4: God and mammon
correct: God and mammon
explanation: Jesus taught that undivided devotion belongs to God, ruling out dual allegiance with wealth. Luke 16:13 (KJV) - "No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon."

question: Why did the Pharisees deride Jesus when they heard his teaching concerning unrighteous mammon and true riches?
opt1: Who were covetous
opt2: Because they were Sadducees who denied the resurrection
opt3: Because they held roman citizenship
opt4: Because they had made vow of voluntary poverty
correct: Who were covetous
explanation: Their inner love of money provoked their mocking derision. Luke 16:14 (KJV) - "And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him."

question: How did Jesus describe the apparel and luxury of the rich man in the narrative of the Rich Man and Lazarus?
opt1: Clothed in armor of brass, feast of wild beasts
opt2: Which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day
opt3: Adorned with gold chains, drank wine from golden cups
opt4: Decked in scarlet robes, attended by fifty guards
correct: Which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day
explanation: The rich man lived in uninterrupted, ostentatious self-indulgence. Luke 16:19 (KJV) - "There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:"

question: Where was the beggar Lazarus carried by the angels when he died?
opt1: Into paradise above the clouds
opt2: Into the third heaven of glory
opt3: Into Abraham's bosom
opt4: To the temple on Mount Zion
correct: Into Abraham's bosom
explanation: Lazarus was transported into the comfort of Abraham's bosom. Luke 16:22 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;"

question: What conclusive answer did Abraham give when the tormented rich man pleaded that Lazarus be sent to warn his five brethren?
opt1: The gates of the underworld are barred forever
opt2: No man may pass from torments unto the land of the living
opt3: Their sins have reached unto heaven and cannot be forgiven
opt4: If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead
correct: If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead
explanation: Scripture's revelation is entirely sufficient; if rejected, even a resurrection will not persuade. Luke 16:31 (KJV) - "And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead."

question: What did Jesus say would be better for a man than that he should offend one of these little ones?
opt1: That a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea
opt2: That he were smitten with perpetual blindness
opt3: That he were driven into the wilderness to dwell with beasts
opt4: That he had never been born into the world
correct: That a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea
explanation: Causing a vulnerable believer to stumble incurs severe judgment. Luke 17:2 (KJV) - "It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones."

question: If a brother trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again saying, 'I repent', what did Jesus command?
opt1: Demand two witnesses before receiving him
opt2: Thou shalt forgive him
opt3: Bring him before the elders of the church
opt4: Require him to offer restitution at the altar
correct: Thou shalt forgive him
explanation: Christ commands boundless willingness to extend forgiveness upon repentance. Luke 17:4 (KJV) - "And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him."

question: If the disciples had faith as a grain of mustard seed, what tree did Jesus say they could command to be plucked up by the root and planted in the sea?
opt1: An olive tree
opt2: A cedar of Lebanon
opt3: This sycamine tree
opt4: A fig tree
correct: This sycamine tree
explanation: Jesus cited the sycamine (mulberry) tree to illustrate faith's power. Luke 17:6 (KJV) - "And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you."

question: What humble acknowledgment did Jesus instruct his servants to make when they have done all those things which are commanded them?
opt1: We have earned our reward among the saints of God
opt2: Our righteousness exceedeth the righteousness of the scribes
opt3: The Lord hath need of our faithful labours
opt4: We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do
correct: We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do
explanation: Total obedience is merely our reasonable obligation, conferring no extra merit. Luke 17:10 (KJV) - "So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do."

question: Of the ten lepers cleansed by Jesus as they went to shew themselves unto the priests, what was the nationality of the only one who returned to give thanks?
opt1: A Samaritan
opt2: A Roman
opt3: A Syrian
opt4: A Galilean
correct: A Samaritan
explanation: The sole grateful leper was a Samaritan stranger. Luke 17:16 (KJV) - "And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan."

question: What piercing question did Jesus ask when only the Samaritan returned to glorify God for his cleansing?
opt1: Why did the priests refuse to bear testimony?
opt2: Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
opt3: Doth not Israel seek healing more than strangers?
opt4: Hath any of the elders believed on me?
correct: Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
explanation: Jesus highlighted the tragic ungratefulness of the nine healed Israelites. Luke 17:17 (KJV) - "And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?"

question: When demanded of the Pharisees when the kingdom of God should come, what did Jesus reply concerning its nature?
opt1: It shall descend with a trumpet from the highest heavens
opt2: It shall be established when David's throne is rebuilt in Zion
opt3: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you
opt4: It cometh when the Roman empire is completely overthrown
correct: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you
explanation: The kingdom of God is primarily an inward, spiritual reality. Luke 17:20-21 (KJV) - "And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you."

question: What two historical judgments from Genesis did Jesus cite to warn of the unexpected suddenness of the coming of the Son of man?
opt1: The destruction of the tower of Babel and the famine of Joseph
opt2: The confusion of tongues and the plague of Egypt
opt3: The fall of Jericho and the defeat of Ai
opt4: The days of Noe (Noah) and the days of Lot
correct: The days of Noe (Noah) and the days of Lot
explanation: Jesus referenced the historical judgment days of Noah and Lot to warn of sudden catastrophe. Luke 17:28 (KJV) - "Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;"

question: What three-word solemn admonition did Jesus give concerning looking back to worldly possessions?
opt1: Remember Lot's wife
opt2: Flee from Sodom
opt3: Watch and pray
opt4: Look not back
correct: Remember Lot's wife
explanation: Jesus warned against fatal attachment to worldly goods with this brief command. Luke 17:32 (KJV) - "Remember Lot's wife."

question: When the disciples asked, 'Where, Lord?' regarding the separation of one being taken and the other left, what proverbial answer did Jesus provide?
opt1: In the valley of Jehoshaphat where the heathen are judged
opt2: Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together
opt3: Upon the Mount of Olives which shall cleave in the midst
opt4: At the four corners of the earth under the sun
correct: Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together
explanation: Divine judgment falls inexorably wherever moral corruption is found. Luke 17:37 (KJV) - "And they answered and said unto him, Where, Lord? And he said unto them, Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together."

question: What central spiritual lesson was the Parable of the Unjust Judge spoken to demonstrate?
opt1: That magistrates should fear God and regard man
opt2: That widows must be supported by the congregation
opt3: That men ought always to pray, and not to faint
opt4: That vengeance belongeth unto the Lord alone
correct: That men ought always to pray, and not to faint
explanation: Luke explicitly defines the parable's purpose: persevering, unceasing prayer. Luke 18:1 (KJV) - "And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;"

question: What description did the unjust judge give of his own character within his heart?
opt1: I am a servant of Caesar and keeper of Roman law
opt2: I am corrupt and take bribes from the wealthy
opt3: I despise the poor and honor only the rulers of Zion
opt4: Though I fear not God, nor regard man
correct: Though I fear not God, nor regard man
explanation: The judge admitted his complete lack of reverent fear toward God or respect for people. Luke 18:4 (KJV) - "And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;"

question: What prayer did the Pharisee pray within himself when he stood in the temple?
opt1: God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess
opt2: Lord, remember my righteousness and bless my household with peace and abundant corn
opt3: I praise thee, Lord God of Abraham, that thou hast chosen me to teach thy holy law
opt4: Hear my supplication, O God, and deliver thy holy city from the oppression of the Gentiles
correct: God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess
explanation: The Pharisee trusted in his own works and boasted self-righteously before God. Luke 18:11-12 (KJV) - "The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess."

question: What prayer did the publican make, standing afar off and smiting upon his breast without lifting up so much as his eyes unto heaven?
opt1: Lord, remember my poverty and forgive my debts
opt2: God be merciful to me a sinner
opt3: Have pity on me, Son of David, and cleanse my transgressions
opt4: O Lord, wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity
correct: God be merciful to me a sinner
explanation: The publican pleaded solely for divine propitiation and mercy. Luke 18:13 (KJV) - "And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner."

question: What did Jesus say regarding how one must receive the kingdom of God in order to enter therein?
opt1: With the wisdom and understanding of the scribes
opt2: Through much fasting and observance of the new moons
opt3: Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein
opt4: By keeping the whole law from his youth up
correct: Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein
explanation: Childlike trust and humility are mandatory to enter God's kingdom. Luke 18:17 (KJV) - "Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein."

question: What did Jesus tell the wealthy ruler was the one thing he still lacked after claiming to have kept all the commandments from his youth?
opt1: Offer a burnt offering of rams in the holy temple
opt2: Confess thy secret faults before the high priest
opt3: Fast forty days in the wilderness as Moses did
opt4: Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me
correct: Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me
explanation: Christ uncovered the ruler's idolatrous attachment to wealth. Luke 18:22 (KJV) - "Now when Jesus heard these things, he said unto him, Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me."

question: What proverbial comparison did Jesus draw to describe the difficulty of a rich man entering the kingdom of God?
opt1: For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God
opt2: It is easier to move a mountain into the midst of the sea
opt3: It is easier for a lion to feed upon straw like an ox
opt4: It is easier to gather spilled water from the sand
correct: For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God
explanation: Humanly speaking, the salvation of the wealthy is impossible. Luke 18:25 (KJV) - "For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."

question: When the hearers asked, 'Who then can be saved?', what comfort did Jesus provide?
opt1: He that endureth unto the end, the same shall be saved
opt2: The things which are impossible with men are possible with God
opt3: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find
opt4: He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life
correct: The things which are impossible with men are possible with God
explanation: Salvation is a divine miracle overcoming human impossibility. Luke 18:27 (KJV) - "And he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God."

question: What title did the blind beggar sitting by the wayside near Jericho cry out when he heard that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by?
opt1: Rabbi, Son of Abraham
opt2: Prophet of the Highest
opt3: Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me
opt4: King of Israel, deliver me
correct: Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me
explanation: The blind man recognized Jesus' Messianic lineage as the Son of David. Luke 18:38 (KJV) - "And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me."

question: What did Jesus say to the blind beggar when restoring his sight outside Jericho?
opt1: Go thy way; wash in the pool of Siloam
opt2: According to the law of Moses, show thyself to the priest
opt3: Thy sins be forgiven thee; rise and walk
opt4: Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee
correct: Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee
explanation: The blind beggar was healed through his faith in Jesus. Luke 18:42 (KJV) - "And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee."

question: Into what kind of tree did Zacchaeus climb to see Jesus in Jericho, because he was little of stature?
opt1: A sycomore tree
opt2: A cedar tree
opt3: A palm tree
opt4: An olive tree
correct: A sycomore tree
explanation: Zacchaeus climbed a sycomore tree to see Jesus over the crowd. Luke 19:4 (KJV) - "And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way."

question: What pledge of restitution did Zacchaeus make to the Lord upon joyfully receiving Jesus into his house?
opt1: Behold, Lord, I offer seven bullocks in the temple and fast forty days
opt2: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold
opt3: I renounce my office as chief publican and donate all my gold to the treasury
opt4: I will give a double tithe of all my income unto the priests of Jericho
correct: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold
explanation: Zacchaeus demonstrated genuine repentance through generous restitution. Luke 19:8 (KJV) - "And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold."

question: What supreme mission statement of Christ's earthly ministry is stated in Luke 19 following Zacchaeus's salvation?
opt1: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly
opt2: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me to heal the brokenhearted
opt3: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost
opt4: I came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil it
correct: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost
explanation: Jesus summarized His core purpose: seeking and saving the lost. Luke 19:10 (KJV) - "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost."

question: In the Parable of the Ten Pounds, what message did the rebellious citizens send after the nobleman into the far country?
opt1: We have no king but Caesar
opt2: Deliver us from the yoke of taxation
opt3: Thy servants have wasted thy silver in riotous living
opt4: We will not have this man to reign over us
correct: We will not have this man to reign over us
explanation: The citizens explicitly rejected the nobleman's royal authority. Luke 19:14 (KJV) - "But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us."

question: What reward did the nobleman give to the first servant whose single pound had gained ten pounds?
opt1: Have thou authority over ten cities
opt2: A golden crown and seat at the king's right hand
opt3: Double portion of all the revenues of the palace
opt4: Ruler over all the treasures of Egypt
correct: Have thou authority over ten cities
explanation: Faithfulness with small entrusted resources is rewarded with civic governance in the kingdom. Luke 19:17 (KJV) - "And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities."

question: What reason did the fearful, slothful servant give for keeping his pound laid up in a napkin?
opt1: Because thieves prowled along the borders of the city
opt2: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow
opt3: Lest the money changers should diminish the silver by usury
opt4: Because the citizens forbade the trading of foreign currency
correct: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow
explanation: The wicked servant mischaracterized his master as harsh and exacting. Luke 19:21 (KJV) - "For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow."

question: What answer did Jesus instruct his disciples to give if anyone asked why they were loosing the colt at Bethphage?
opt1: The King of Glory hath commanded it
opt2: The prophets foretold that Zion's King should ride thereon
opt3: Because the Lord hath need of him
opt4: It shall be returned before the evening sacrifice
correct: Because the Lord hath need of him
explanation: The simple authority of the Lord was sufficient. Luke 19:31 (KJV) - "And if any man ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say unto him, Because the Lord hath need of him."

question: What did Jesus answer the Pharisees who demanded that he rebuke his disciples for their loud Messianic praises during the descent of the Mount of Olives?
opt1: Suffer them to speak, for they fulfill the words of David
opt2: Their voices cannot be silenced by the commandments of men
opt3: The angels of heaven join their chorus of praise
opt4: I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out
correct: I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out
explanation: Creation itself would testify if human voices were silenced. Luke 19:40 (KJV) - "And he answered and said unto them, I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out."

question: What did Jesus do when he came near and beheld the city of Jerusalem?
opt1: He wept over it
opt2: He offered a sacrifice of praise upon Mount Olivet
opt3: He cursed its gates with perpetual desolation
opt4: He sounded a silver trumpet toward the temple
correct: He wept over it
explanation: Jesus wept over Jerusalem in grief for its impending destruction. Luke 19:41 (KJV) - "And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,"

question: What declaration did Jesus make as he cast out them that sold and bought in the temple?
opt1: Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise
opt2: It is written, My house is the house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of thieves
opt3: The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up
opt4: Holiness becometh thine house, O Lord, for ever

question: In the Parable of the Vineyard, what did the husbandmen say among themselves when they saw the beloved son sent by the lord of the vineyard?

question: Which Jewish sect came to Jesus posing a hypothetical dilemma of seven brothers married successively to one woman, because they denied the resurrection?

question: According to Jesus' answer to the Sadducees, what state do those accounted worthy to obtain that world and the resurrection from the dead enter into regarding marriage and mortality?

question: What question from Psalm 110 did Jesus propose to the scribes regarding Christ's identity?

question: What four outward practices of the scribes did Jesus warn his disciples to beware of?

question: What prophecy did Jesus utter regarding the temple's magnificent stones and gifts when some spoke of them?

question: What constant duty did Jesus enjoin upon his followers to escape the impending tribulations and stand before the Son of man?
